myth: Cracking your knuckles causes arthritis
fact: Studies show no link between knuckle cracking and arthritis.

myth: You lose most of your body heat through your head
fact: Heat loss is proportional to exposed skin and the head is only about 10% of body surface.

myth: Sugar makes children hyperactive
fact: Multiple studies find no link between sugar and hyperactivity in children.

myth: Reading in dim light ruins your eyesight
fact: Dim light can cause eye strain but no permanent vision damage.

myth: You should drink eight glasses of water a day
fact: The eight glasses rule is a myth and needs vary by body activity and climate.

myth: The tongue map shows only four taste zones
fact: Taste buds across the whole tongue detect all five basic tastes.

myth: The Great Wall of China is visible from space
fact: The Great Wall is barely visible from low orbit and not visible from the Moon.

myth: The Sun is yellow
fact: The Sun is white and Earth's atmosphere scatters blue light making it look yellow.

myth: There is no gravity in space
fact: Astronauts float because they are in continuous free fall around Earth.

myth: The Moon has a permanent dark side
fact: The far side gets sunlight and is far not dark.

myth: Mercury is the hottest planet
fact: Venus at about 465°C is hotter due to a runaway greenhouse effect.

myth: The Eiffel Tower grows taller in summer
fact: Heat expands the iron adding up to 15 cm in summer.

myth: Napoleon was very short
fact: Napoleon was about 5'7 average for his time and the short myth came from British propaganda.

myth: Vikings wore horned helmets
fact: No archaeological evidence supports it and the image came from 19th century romanticism.

myth: Marie Antoinette said Let them eat cake
fact: The phrase appears in Rousseau's writings before her time.

myth: The Great Pyramid was built by slaves
fact: Evidence suggests paid skilled laborers built it.

myth: Einstein failed math in school
fact: He excelled in math and the myth stemmed from a mistaken grading report.

myth: More megapixels always mean better photos
fact: Sensor size lens and processing matter as much as pixel count.

myth: You should fully drain your phone battery before charging
fact: Modern lithium-ion batteries prefer partial charges and draining regularly shortens life.

myth: Private browsing makes you invisible online
fact: It hides history locally but not from your ISP or websites.

myth: Macs cannot get viruses
fact: Macs can be infected though macOS has fewer malware threats than Windows.

myth: Goldfish have a three second memory
fact: Goldfish can remember things for months and learn tasks.

myth: Bulls are enraged by the color red
fact: Bulls are colorblind and charge because of the cape's movement.

myth: Ostriches bury their heads in the sand
fact: Ostriches lie flat or dig nests and never bury their heads.

myth: A duck's quack does not echo
fact: A duck's quack does echo and the myth came from a TV segment.

myth: Honey never spoils
fact: Sealed honey can last indefinitely and edible honey was found in Egyptian tombs.

myth: Eating carrots improves your night vision
fact: Carrots provide vitamin A for eye health but cannot give night vision.

myth: MSG is harmful to your health
fact: MSG is generally recognized as safe and Chinese restaurant syndrome is unproven.

myth: You should wait an hour after eating before swimming
fact: No medical evidence supports a dangerous cramp risk.

myth: The five second rule keeps food safe
fact: Bacteria transfer in milliseconds and there is no safe window.

myth: We only use 10% of our brains
fact: Brain imaging shows activity across nearly all regions during the day.

myth: People are either left brained or right brained
fact: Both hemispheres work together for most tasks.
